I took on one of those "freezer food challenges" with this shopping list and it worked rather well. The plan is enough for 50 meals, but only around 30 fit in a normal freezer, so that's what I did: http://happymoneysaver.com/making-50-freezer-meals-in-one-day/

Warning: This is not for the faint of heart. It actually took me two days to get through all the cooking, not one. I was really burned out at the end and hated all things food. But, we had enough meals to eat off of for two weeks. Plus all the extra left-over ingredients we used to make lunches or to build up our pantry. A very good investment if you are feeding a family.

**Grocery List:**

Chicken Breast (24 breasts)

Rotisserie Chicken (1 - I shredded all the meat)

Pork chops (8 chops, bone-in)

Beef Stew Meat (1lb)

Ground Beef (1lb)

Sausage 2 packages

Bacon (I ended up using bacon bits instead)

Hasbrowns 2 - 16 oz bags

Pie Crust (2 frozen, then one can of rolled Pillsbury dough in the tube for the tops)

Corn tortillas

Green chilies

Jumbo Pasta Shells (36 shells, about 4 boxes)

Lasagna Noodles

Pesto

Pinapple (we were out of control and bought a 6lb can, don't do this we only used about two servings)

Tomato Sauces (15 oz can)

Flour Tortillas

Corn tortillas

Chicken Broth (1 large can or box)

Eggs (2 dozen)

Cottage Cheese (2pts)

Cream Cheese (12oz)

Parmesan/Asiago (3 cups)

Shredded Cheddar Cheese (3 cups)

Shredded Mozzarella (24oz)

Sour Cream (3 cups)

Butter

Milk

Frozen Peas

Shredded Carrots (1 cup)

Cilantro (2 cups)

Green Onions (24)

Bag of Onions (used in various recipes)

Large Potatoes (12)

Lime Juice (~7 limes)

Beef Bouillon powder

Dijon mustered

Fried Rice Seasoning

Garlic Salt

Gravy Mix (2 packages)

Toasted almond slivers

Honey

Soy Sauce

Corn Starch

Canola Oil

Sugar

Ketchup

Vinegar

Ginger

Cinnamon

Ground Cloves

Coke

Marinara Sauce (a couple jars)

Enchilada Sauce

Aluminum baking trays (4 of them from the 99 cents store)

Aluminum foil, and freezer bags...lots of them!

**Meals:**

Honey Lime Chicken (1 dinner)

Homemade Pot Pies (2 dinners)

Chicken Fried Rice (1 dinner)

Twice Baked Potato (24 servings)

Sweet and Sour Chicken (2 dinners) <-my favorite!

Honey Spice Glazed Pork Chops (2 dinners) <-my husbands favorite, ate them while watching Ronin, said it was every mans dream.

Pesto Chicken Stuffed Shells (2 dinners)

Cilantro Lime Chicken Tacos (1 dinner)

Cafe Rio Pulled Pork (1 dinner)

Chicken Enchiladas (1 dinner)

Lasagna (2 dinners)

Breakfast Burritos

Typo. I just copy and paste from my excel sheet. I type out every ingredient per recipe and then sort by ingredient. So chicken breasts might appear four times if it was in four different recipes. I went through and tried to delete the dups, guess I missed some!

BTW, mixed bean soup would make a great addition to the list. Just get one of those bags of '15 beans.'

1) Soak beans in water overnight
2) In the morning, drain and refill with fresh water
3) Toss in the crockpot for roughly 6-8 hours while periodically seasoning it.
4) 30 minutes before serving, toss in some kielbasa (optional)
5) Right before serving, toss in a small amount of brown sugar
6) Serve mixed with mixed with rice (optional) (cook separately)

Typical spices and seasoning includes salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper, red pepper, oregano, etc.
